title: Design a Parking Lot
relevance: High — the canonical first LLD / machine-coding question (campus + experienced); Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon, Microsoft, Atlassian, Walmart, Adobe, and most Indian product cos use it to probe OOP, SOLID, Strategy/Factory, and concurrency.
company_notes: Extremely common first campus/new-grad LLD or timed CLI machine-coding round in India (Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon, Walmart, Razorpay, Atlassian-style); experienced/SDE-2 keeps the same domain with harder concurrency, Strategy vs inheritance, payment, Observer boards, and allocation follow-ups; FAANG OOD whiteboard (Google/Meta lore) emphasizes clarifying questions and clean class model over CLI I/O; among the most asked LLD problems and a template for later ones (elevator, Splitwise, booking).

phases.goal: Lock mandatory park/unpark/display flows, common extensions, NFRs, and stated assumptions before designing classes.

must_hit.point: Mandatory FR: multi-floor lot; park assigns a typed spot and ticket; unpark by ticket; show free/occupied counts (optionally slot lists) per floor × type.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists create multi-floor lot, park→typed spot+ticket, unpark by ticket, and display free/occupied per floor and vehicle type.

must_hit.point: State common extensions to ask: hourly fee + payment, multiple gates, EV/handicapped spots, reject when full, admin add floor/slot.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate asks whether fees/payment, multi-gate, EV/accessible spots, full-lot rejection, and admin floor/slot add are in scope.

must_hit.point: NFR: correct under concurrent park/unpark; extensible for new vehicle types and allocation/pricing strategies; modular files; working demo/CLI.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate calls out concurrency correctness, strategy extensibility, no god class, and a working demo.

must_hit.point: Assumptions: one physical lot (or inject lot id); spot↔vehicle type mapping fixed unless told otherwise; no reservations unless asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate explicitly states single-lot (or lot id), fixed type mapping, and no reservations by default.

probes: Before drawing classes, what functional and non-functional requirements would you clarify for this parking lot?
Which use cases must the system support on day one versus only if asked?

hints.1: Start by listing customer enter/exit and admin/display flows before naming classes.
hints.2: Separate mandatory FR (multi-floor park/unpark/display) from optional fee, gates, EV, and admin extensions.
hints.3: Mandatory: multi-floor, park→typed spot+ticket, unpark by ticket, free/occupied per floor×type; NFR: concurrency, strategy extensibility, modular CLI demo; assume one lot, fixed type mapping, no reservations.

phases.goal: Name the core domain objects and their relationships (composition vs inheritance) without jumping into full API detail.

must_hit.point: Core composition: ParkingLot (one) contains many ParkingFloor, each containing many ParkingSpot.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate draws ParkingLot → ParkingFloor → ParkingSpot as a HAS-A hierarchy.

must_hit.point: Vehicle hierarchy plus Ticket holding entry time, spot, and vehicle; optional Gate, Payment, DisplayBoard.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names Vehicle subtypes, Ticket fields (entry time/spot/vehicle), and may mention Gate/Payment/DisplayBoard as optional.

must_hit.point: IS-A vs HAS-A: inherit Vehicle (and optionally typed ParkingSpot); compose floors into the lot; inject strategies rather than subclass ParkingLot per pricing rule.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate says Vehicle is inheritance, floors are composition, and pricing/allocation are injected strategies not ParkingLot subclasses.

probes: What are the core entities and how do they relate—composition versus inheritance?
What belongs on a Ticket versus on ParkingLot or ParkingSpot?

hints.1: Name the nouns first: lot, floor, spot, vehicle, ticket.
hints.2: Show ParkingLot owns floors owns spots; Vehicle is a type hierarchy; Ticket links vehicle, spot, and entry time.
hints.3: ParkingLot (1) → ParkingFloor (many) → ParkingSpot (many); Vehicle hierarchy; Ticket(entry time, spot, vehicle); optional Gate/Payment/DisplayBoard; inject strategies, don't subclass the lot per pricing rule.

phases.goal: Produce a class model with Facade-style ParkingLot, strategies, and clear ownership of spots, tickets, and optional observers/gates.

must_hit.point: ParkingLot is the Facade entry point holding floors, SpotAllocationStrategy, PricingStrategy, and the active ticket registry.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate shows ParkingLot.park/unpark orchestrating floors and strategies with an active tickets map.

must_hit.point: ParkingFloor owns spots and free lists/heaps per type; ParkingSpot is a free↔occupied state machine with type check on assign.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate assigns free-slot tracking to the floor and free/occupied + type check to the spot.

must_hit.point: Patterns that earn points: Strategy (fee + allocation), Factory (Vehicle/Spot from type), Facade (park/unpark), optional Singleton for one lot, Observer for display boards.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names Strategy, Factory, Facade, and optionally Singleton/Observer with the right responsibility each.

must_hit.point: SOLID: OCP for new vehicle/fee/allocation without editing ParkingLot; SRP split lot/floor/strategy; DIP on PricingStrategy and SpotAllocationStrategy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate ties OCP/SRP/DIP to strategies and not putting billing logic inside ParkingLot.

probes: Sketch the class diagram and where Strategy, Factory, and Facade sit.
Who owns free-slot tracking, and who calculates fees?

hints.1: Think of ParkingLot as a thin orchestrator, not a god class.
hints.2: Wire ParkingLot to SpotAllocationStrategy and PricingStrategy; floors own spots; tickets stay in an active map.
hints.3: ParkingLot Facade holds floors + strategies + tickets; Floor maintains free lists/heaps per type; Spot assign/release with type check; name Strategy/Factory/Facade (and optional Singleton/Observer).

phases.goal: Define the park/unpark/display API, default allocation rule, ticket lifecycle, and availability query behavior.

must_hit.point: API surface: create_parking_lot; park_vehicle → Ticket or FULL; unpark_vehicle → VehicleInfo or INVALID; display free_count | free_slots | occupied_slots by vehicleType.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists create/park/unpark/display with FULL and INVALID outcomes matching the machine-coding CLI shape.

must_hit.point: Default allocation: same type, lowest floor, lowest slot number; ticket lifecycle park → issue id → active map → unpark by id → fee → free spot → invalidate; ticket format often {lotId}_{floor}_{slot}.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate states lowest-floor/lowest-slot same-type allocation and the full ticket issue/lookup/invalidate flow, optionally with lotId_floor_slot ids.

must_hit.point: Maintain free counts or free-slot lists/heaps per floor × vehicle type so display/park do not scan all spots when claiming scale.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate keeps per floor×type free counts or free-slot structures instead of rescanning every spot.

must_hit.point: If scale is pushed: spot count can be hundreds to tens of thousands (Educative cites ~40k); allocation should be O(log n) per type via heap/TreeSet, not an O(n) full scan.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate mentions in-memory is fine at that scale and free-slot heap/TreeSet for O(log n) allocation.

probes: Walk through park and unpark end to end, including what the ticket stores.
How do you choose a spot by default, and how does display stay cheap?

hints.1: Implement the mandatory CLI happy path before optional fees or fancy allocation.
hints.2: Park finds same-type lowest floor/slot, issues a ticket into an active map; unpark looks up by id, frees the spot, invalidates the ticket.
hints.3: create/park/unpark/display API; default same type + lowest floor + lowest slot; ticket {lotId}_{floor}_{slot}; free structures per floor×type; O(log n) heap/TreeSet if scale is discussed (~40k spots).

phases.goal: Show Strategy-based allocation and pricing so new vehicle types, fees, and policies plug in without editing ParkingLot.

must_hit.point: SpotAllocationStrategy so nearest-entrance or even-fill is a new class, not an if inside ParkingLot; default remains same type, lowest floor, lowest slot.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate extracts allocation behind a strategy interface and gives nearest-entrance/even-fill as alternate implementations.

must_hit.point: PricingStrategy.calculate(ticket, exitTime) for hourly/flat/vehicle-type/EV surcharge — never hardcode rates inside unpark.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate puts fee calculation on PricingStrategy and refuses to embed rates in unpark.

must_hit.point: Enum vs hierarchy for Vehicle/Spot: enum is faster; abstract subtypes win OCP when behavior diverges (e.g. EV charging); prefer hierarchy in OOD, enum OK if timeboxed with centralized mapping.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate compares enum speed vs hierarchy OCP and picks based on round type/timebox.

must_hit.point: Singleton ParkingLot is common in tutorials but prefer injecting a single instance for testability unless the interviewer wants classic Singleton; multi-lot needs a repository keyed by id, not a process-wide Singleton.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate criticizes process-wide Singleton for testability/multi-lot and suggests DI or ParkingLotRepository.

probes: How would you change allocation to nearest-to-entrance without rewriting ParkingLot?
Where should hourly vs flat vs weekend pricing live, and how do you add EV spots?

hints.1: Anything that might change—how we pick spots or how we price—should not be an if-ladder in the lot.
hints.2: Introduce SpotAllocationStrategy and PricingStrategy plugged at construction (OCP).
hints.3: New allocation/pricing = new strategy class; EV/handicapped = new spot subtype + allocation filter; prefer DI over Singleton for multi-lot/testability.

phases.goal: Prevent double-booking under multi-gate park/unpark and keep locks off the fee-calculation hot path where possible.

must_hit.point: Two gates must not assign the same spot: race on read-then-write; need synchronized assign or atomic find+occupy under one critical section.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate names the double-booking race and protects find+occupy as one critical section.

must_hit.point: Prefer fine-grained locks (per floor / per spot type) or ConcurrentHashMap for active tickets; coarse synchronized on the whole lot works for demos but bottlenecks under multi-gate load.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate contrasts whole-lot synchronized with per-floor/per-type locks and a concurrent ticket map.

must_hit.point: Multi-gate scaling: do not lock the entire lot for fee calculation; only for assign/release and ticket map update; free-slot heap/TreeSet per floor×type under contention.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate scopes locks to assign/release/ticket updates and keeps fee calc outside the global lock.

probes: Two cars enter at once — how do you ensure they cannot get the same spot?
What would you lock under multi-gate load, and what would you leave unlocked?

hints.1: Think about the race between checking a spot is free and marking it occupied.
hints.2: Make find-and-occupy atomic; mention per-floor locks as better than locking the whole lot.
hints.3: Atomic find+occupy (or synchronized assign); ConcurrentHashMap for tickets; fine-grained per-floor/per-type locks; fee calculation outside the global lock; free-slot heap/TreeSet under contention.

tradeoffs.topic: Enum vs class hierarchy for Vehicle/Spot
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Enum is faster to code; abstract class/subtypes win OCP when behavior diverges (e.g. EV charging). Prefer hierarchy in OOD rounds; enum OK if timeboxed with centralized mapping.

tradeoffs.topic: Allocation Strategy vs hardcoded lowest-floor scan
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Hardcoded lowest-floor/lowest-slot scan passes tests; SpotAllocationStrategy is the expected extensibility answer when allocation policy must change (nearest entrance, even fill).
synchronized park() is correct but serializes gates; per-floor/per-type locks or compare-and-set on spot occupancy show senior thinking — call out the double-booking race explicitly.

Singleton is common in tutorials; prefer injecting a single instance for testability unless the interviewer wants classic Singleton; multi-lot drops process-wide Singleton for a repository keyed by id.

gotchas.trap: Assuming a car can take a truck spot (or vice versa) without asking
gotchas.correction: Product rule; default is exact type match; size hierarchy is a deliberate extension.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring the two-cars-same-spot race under concurrent entry
gotchas.correction: Race on read-then-write; show synchronized assign or atomic occupy.

gotchas.trap: Adding EV charging / handicapped spots via endless switch inside ParkingLot
gotchas.correction: New spot subtype plus allocation filter; do not switch forever inside ParkingLot.

gotchas.trap: Hardcoding hourly vs flat vs weekend pricing in unpark
gotchas.correction: Swap PricingStrategy; receipt can include breakdown.

gotchas.trap: Using a process-wide Singleton when asked for multiple parking lots / multi-city
gotchas.correction: Drop process-wide Singleton; use ParkingLotRepository keyed by id.

gotchas.trap: Implementing nearest-to-entrance by editing ParkingLot conditionals
gotchas.correction: New SpotAllocationStrategy using spot distance/id order; heap by distance.

gotchas.trap: God-class ParkingLot that also bills, prints, and persists
gotchas.correction: Split by SRP or the interviewer docks design score.

gotchas.trap: Finishing optional extensibility but failing mandatory park/unpark/display
gotchas.correction: Mandatory first: park, unpark, and display before optional features.
